thesis.one_sentence: The mathematical structure of physical law is isomorphic to the structure of spiritual reality, with free-will modifiers as the only asymmetry, and the unprovability of the ground from within the system is the signature of the foundational, pointing to a non-physical, necessary, non-formal, self-grounding ground that matches the classical definition of God.

claims.claim: Every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart, differing only by a free-will modifier.
claims.evidence: Presentation of ten paired equations (e.g., Newton's law vs. Grace equation, QCD potential vs. Love binding equation) with explicit asymmetry terms.
claims.assumption: The spiritual domain exists and is structured analogously to the physical domain.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The claim asserts structural identity based on formal similarity of equations, but no empirical evidence is provided that the spiritual equations actually govern any observable spiritual phenomena.

claims.claim: The Master Equation χ = ∭(G·M·E·S·T·K·R·Q·F·C) dxdydt integrates all ten laws and shows that at full coherence, physical and spiritual coherence are mathematically identical (χ = C).
claims.evidence: Presentation of the integral equation and the statement that at Law 10, the asymmetry terms vanish.
claims.assumption: The ten variables can be meaningfully multiplied and integrated across a configuration space.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: No operational definitions are given for the variables G, M, E, etc.; the integral is purely formal with no units, no boundary conditions, and no empirical referent.

claims.claim: The Terminus Sui theorem proves that all closed systems fail to self-complete, requiring an external ground.
claims.evidence: Reference to five proven theorems, but no proof is given in the document.
claims.assumption: The referenced theorems are correctly proven and applicable to the systems under discussion.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The document asserts the theorem as proven but provides no proof, relying on external reference that is not accessible in the text.

claims.claim: The properties of the required external ground (G1-G5: External, Sufficient, Costly, Merit-independent, Temporally prior) can be derived from the failure conditions of closed systems.
claims.evidence: Logical derivation from the Terminus Sui theorem and the structure of the Master Equation.
claims.assumption: The failure conditions of closed systems uniquely determine these five properties.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The derivation is not shown step-by-step; the properties are asserted as necessary but alternative properties are not ruled out.

claims.claim: Shannon entropy equation H = -∑p_i log p_i is literally the Logos information equation, because information IS Logos.
claims.evidence: The equation is presented without modification, and the claim is that it is the same equation.
claims.assumption: The concept of Logos in theology is identical to the mathematical concept of information.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The claim equates a mathematical formalism with a theological concept without any bridging argument; it asserts identity based on identical notation.

claims.claim: The Unprovability Theorem shows that any truly foundational ground G must be unprovable from within the system S that it grounds.
claims.evidence: A six-step proof is given in the document.
claims.assumption: The proof's logical steps are valid and the definitions of 'ground' and 'provable' are consistent.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The proof relies on an informal definition of 'ground' that may not be rigorous; the conclusion that unprovability is the signature of the foundational is a philosophical interpretation, not a mathematical necessity.

claims.claim: The constraint chain (non-physical, non-contingent, non-formal, self-grounding) yields the classical definition of God.
claims.evidence: Logical derivation from the Unprovability Theorem and the properties of the ground.
claims.assumption: The classical definition of God (Aristotle, Aquinas, Anselm) is correctly captured by these four properties.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The claim that these properties uniquely define God is not argued; other entities (e.g., a Platonic Form) could also satisfy them.

claims.claim: The Maxwell-Truth parallel shows the same four-equation structure, piece for piece, with acceptance factor A as the only asymmetry.
claims.evidence: Reference to the Maxwell-Truth parallel, but no equations are shown in the document.
claims.assumption: The parallel is exact and not merely metaphorical.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: No evidence is provided; the claim is asserted without demonstration.

claims.claim: The self-recursive structure of the Master Equation means that equilibrium (dχ/dt = 0) is the mathematical condition for salvation.
claims.evidence: Presentation of the unified field equation dχ/dt = G_ext·η(K) - λS(χ) and the equilibrium condition.
claims.assumption: The concept of salvation can be meaningfully mapped to a mathematical equilibrium condition.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The mapping from a differential equation to a theological concept is asserted without justification; no empirical or logical bridge is provided.

claims.claim: The soteriological limit ∫G_ext dt → ∞ for χ(∞) > 0 shows that only an infinite source of Grace qualifies, which is the mathematical statement of exactly one theological position.
claims.evidence: The integral condition is stated and interpreted.
claims.assumption: The integral of Grace over time is a well-defined mathematical quantity that can be infinite.
claims.overclaim_diagnosis: The claim that this uniquely corresponds to one theological position (presumably Christianity) is not argued; other religions also posit infinite sources of grace or merit.

explicit.definition: The principle that no closed system can complete itself; five theorems prove this.
χ = ∭(G·M·E·S·T·K·R·Q·F·C) dxdydt — coherence integrated across space and time.
External, Sufficient, Costly, Merit-independent, Temporally prior.
Any truly foundational ground G must be unprovable from within the system S that it grounds.
The ground must be non-physical, non-contingent, non-formal, self-grounding.

implied.usage_implies: A measure of integration or harmony, both physical and spiritual, that can be quantified and integrated.
The information structure of reality, equated with Shannon entropy and Kolmogorov complexity.
A state of equilibrium where grace input balances entropy production.
A decay process analogous to beta decay, with a rate given by a quantum field-theoretic formula.

assumptions.assumption: The spiritual domain exists and is structured analogously to the physical domain.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The entire framework collapses because there is no domain for the spiritual equations to describe.

assumptions.assumption: Mathematical equations can be meaningfully applied to spiritual concepts without empirical validation.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The ten laws become mere metaphors, not structural identities.

assumptions.assumption: The Terminus Sui theorems are correctly proven and applicable.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The argument for an external ground loses its foundation.

assumptions.assumption: The free-will modifiers (R, B, F, W, etc.) are the only differences between physical and spiritual laws.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The claimed isomorphism is incomplete or incorrect.

assumptions.assumption: The integral in the Master Equation is well-defined and convergent.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The Master Equation is not a valid mathematical expression.

assumptions.assumption: The classical definition of God (Aristotle, Aquinas, Anselm) is correctly captured by the four properties.
assumptions.if_this_fails: The constraint chain may point to something other than God.

premises: P1: All closed systems fail to self-complete (Terminus Sui).
P2: Physical laws are mathematically structured and govern physical reality.
P3: Every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart with a free-will modifier.
P4: The Master Equation integrates all laws and shows convergence of physical and spiritual coherence.
P5: The ground of any system must be unprovable from within that system (Unprovability Theorem).
P6: The properties of the ground can be derived from the failure conditions of closed systems.
intermediate_conclusions: IC1: Physical reality requires an external ground to maintain coherence.
IC2: The spiritual domain is governed by the same mathematical structure as the physical domain.
IC3: The ground must be non-physical, necessary, non-formal, and self-grounding.
IC4: The ground matches the classical definition of God.
argument_structure.final_conclusion: The mathematical structure of reality points to a non-physical, necessary, self-grounding ground that is the Logos, and the unprovability of this ground from within the system is the signature of its foundational nature.
argument_structure.weakest_link: The claim that every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart (P3) is asserted without empirical evidence and relies on metaphorical interpretation.
unproven_jumps: From formal similarity of equations to structural identity of domains.
From the Unprovability Theorem to the existence of a specific ground (God).
From the Master Equation to the mathematical condition for salvation.
From the soteriological limit to a specific theological position.

overclaim_detection.diagnosis: The document claims that every physical law has a spiritual counterpart, but only nine are presented (plus the Master Equation), and the selection is not justified as exhaustive.

The document claims that the properties of the ground (non-physical, necessary, etc.) are derived from the failure conditions, but does not show that these properties are uniquely determined or that they cause the ground to be God.
The Master Equation is presented as a mathematical model of reality, but no empirical data or validation is provided to show that it corresponds to actual physical or spiritual phenomena.
The document defines the ground in terms of unprovability and then claims to have discovered that this ground matches God, but the definition is tailored to produce that result.

overclaim_detection.location: Part Nine, For the Person Who Already Believes
overclaim_detection.diagnosis: The document claims that the framework shows faith is rational, but does not provide any practical guidance or evidence that the framework changes actual belief or practice.

addressed: The objection that the framework does not prove God (addressed in Part Eight, Unprovability Theorem).
The objection that the equations are merely metaphorical (implicitly addressed by claiming structural identity).
missing: The objection that the spiritual variables (Grace, Sin, Faith, etc.) are not operationally defined and cannot be measured.
The objection that the free-will modifiers are ad hoc additions with no empirical basis.
The objection that the framework is unfalsifiable because it makes no testable predictions.
The objection that the mathematical formalism is being applied to domains where it has no meaning (category error).
The objection that the Terminus Sui theorems are not proven in the document and may not apply to the systems discussed.
counterarguments.smartest_critic_would_say: Your entire framework rests on the assumption that spiritual concepts like grace, sin, and faith can be meaningfully assigned mathematical values and plugged into equations derived from physics. But you have provided no operational definitions, no measurement procedures, and no empirical evidence that these quantities exist or behave according to your equations. Without that, your 'structural identity' is just a series of analogies dressed in mathematical notation — a beautiful metaphor, not a scientific or mathematical discovery.

kill_conditions_stated: If a closed system could be shown to self-complete, the Terminus Sui theorem would be falsified.
If a physical law were found that has no spiritual counterpart, the isomorphism claim would be weakened.
kill_conditions_missing: If the spiritual variables (Grace, Sin, etc.) cannot be measured or defined operationally, the framework is unfalsifiable.
If the Master Equation makes no testable predictions, it is not a scientific theory.
If the free-will modifiers cannot be independently verified, they are ad hoc.

novelty.what_is_new: The claim that every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart with a free-will modifier, and that the Master Equation integrates them into a unified framework that points to a specific theological conclusion.
novelty.closest_existing_work: Theological physics or 'theophysics' as explored by thinkers like John Polkinghorne or in the 'fine-tuning' arguments, but with a more formal mathematical structure.

compression.one_sentence: The mathematical structure of physical law is isomorphic to the structure of spiritual reality, with free-will modifiers as the only asymmetry, and the unprovability of the ground from within the system is the signature of the foundational, pointing to a non-physical, necessary, non-formal, self-grounding ground that matches the classical definition of God.
compression.three_sentences: The document presents a framework called Theophysics, which claims that every physical law has a structurally identical spiritual counterpart, differing only by a free-will modifier. It argues that all closed systems require an external ground (Terminus Sui), and that the properties of this ground can be derived to match the classical definition of God. The framework concludes that the mathematical structure of reality points to a non-physical, necessary, self-grounding ground (the Logos), and that the unprovability of this ground from within the system is the signature of its foundational nature.
compression.strongest_defensible_version: The document presents a formal analogy between physical laws and spiritual concepts, using mathematical notation to express the analogy, and argues that the structure of physical law requires an external ground that has properties consistent with the classical definition of God.
compression.weakest_version_still_true: The document presents a series of mathematical analogies between physical laws and spiritual concepts, and argues that the unprovability of a foundational ground from within a system is a necessary feature of that ground.
